pr.title: Keep new goal baseline aligned with same-day weight corrections
pr.body:
## Summary

Saving or correcting today's weight after creating a goal could leave its starting weight stale. Web/mobile, Wear and imported weights now align the current goal's baseline within their weight transaction, preserving goal identity, start day, target, pace and history. The goal sync event includes the final safety-review state.

The existing goal start day (`created_at` in the account timezone), metric date and acceptance-local day must match. The timezone is reread after acquiring the shared planning lock; competing weight writers take that lock before metric rows. A late first offline replay saves its metric without changing an older baseline, while committed retries retain their original result.

Closes #446.

## Test plan

| Scenario | Expected and observed result | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Create a 90 kg goal, save 85 kg that day, reload Progress | The same goal starts at 85 kg with 0% progress. Before retained 90 kg / 33%; After shows the correction. | Matched browser captures below; maintained metric regression. |
| Save weight before goal creation, or while goal creation holds the planning lock | Both orders establish the new baseline without changing target, pace, date or completed food-day history. | PostgreSQL smoke. |
| Change timezone while a weight writer waits; test LA/UTC in both directions with explicit/default dates | Eligibility and default date use the committed timezone, and retries retain the receipt. | Forced PostgreSQL overlap and controlled-clock route tests. |
| Overlap web and Wear weight writes in both orders | No lock inversion; successful same-day writes correct the baseline and sync it once. Stale Wear revisions return 409; historical Wear writes retain the baseline. Wear parses date syntax first; the locked timezone decides eligibility in both directions. Newly future dates are rejected without metric/baseline/sync writes; newly current dates are accepted and correct the baseline. | Forced PostgreSQL overlap. |
| Import a current-day weight, overwrite it, KEEP it, or repeat a historical/identical import | Only accepted current-day weight writes correct the baseline. KEEP, historical rows and identical repeats produce no extra goal correction events. After a concurrent timezone change, accepted/skipped rows, counts and future warnings use the locked account day. | Actual import route and ZIP parser in PostgreSQL smoke. |
| Replay after midnight, retry after a newer correction, use pounds, fail sync or make a plan unsafe | No historical/stale overwrite; canonical precision, atomic rollback and existing safety-review behavior are preserved. | Maintained backend regressions. |

Validation: 61 targeted backend tests passed during the writer-path fixes; the final affected Wear suite (14 tests), import suite (6 tests) and backend typecheck passed after their narrow follow-ups. [Current-head PostgreSQL validation passed](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/actions/runs/37828422760), including all concurrency and both-direction timezone cases. All current-head hosted checks passed: 10 successful, 14 path-filtered skips. [Configured review completed with no major issues](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/449#issuecomment-6067011549) at this head; all seven prior findings have verified dispositions and resolved threads. Earlier unchanged-client validation passed 35 client tests, both Expo builds and two browser captures; those unaffected suites were not repeated. Native device testing is deferred; independent QA remains pending.

The screenshots show a synthetic API correction followed by the actual Progress UI reload. They use the real metric route with synthetic persistence; unrelated trend/target/projection values are fixtures. They do not establish native or real database behavior.

Before/base: `4cbcbc740fbe5fa5646b4de31951c79a653176d5`. Captured After: `eb142dd0bcc527398e83b91d29d4514fd9b4e516`. Current head: `650862e1c13be66fe5ec05495320cc66ac32f8bb`. Later fixes preserve the captured stable-timezone scenario; the old images are not relabeled as new-head captures.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: stale 90 kg baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4/before.png) | ![After: corrected 85 kg baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4/after.png) |

[Original captures, build manifests and immutable provenance](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/tree/ce02f46f2d6b3794d3911a74a7c29a63ac6960c4) and [final source binding, review-fix evidence and capture applicability](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/458ff9fa117ca51b2c07c565069d809ecb8518d5/final-source-binding.md) are retained outside product history. issue.title: Update a new goal’s starting weight when today’s weight changes

labels.name: needs-scoping
labels.description: Needs value, scope, acceptance criteria or authorization before agent dispatch.

issue.body:
## Problem

When a goal starts today and today's weight is entered or corrected afterward, the goal can retain an outdated starting weight. The user expects either input order to produce the same goal baseline without restarting the goal.

## Requirements and acceptance

- For the current goal, correct its starting baseline only when its existing start day (created_at in the user timezone), the affected metric date and the current user-local day all match at the first accepted mutation. Preserve the existing date model; no scheduling or backdating is added.
- Preserve goal identity, start date, target, pace and prior history. Do not restart the goal or change older goals, unrelated days or unrelated users.
- Define the existing app's authoritative day/timezone and weight-upsert semantics before implementation. Cover midnight/timezone boundaries and repeated updates using the current rules; do not introduce a new timezone model.
- Preserve units and canonical weight precision. Goal calculations, nutrition/energy projections and displayed baseline must agree with the persisted corrected weight.
- Keep offline edits/sync/retries idempotent. A first replay after the eligible day saves the metric normally without rewriting an older baseline. A retry of an already committed operation retains its original result. Do not add client intent timestamps or historical baseline recalculation.
- Validate both input orders, correction/reload, unit conversion, older-goal and unrelated-day controls, and applicable offline/retry behavior with anonymous synthetic data. No personal health details in public evidence.

## Implementation plan

Use the existing idempotent metric-save transaction. Acquire the shared calorie-planning lock before reading/writing the metric or current goal, resolve eligibility after waiting for the lock, update only start_weight_grams, and emit its goal sync change atomically with the metric. Compute progress and plan safety from the corrected baseline; retain goal identity, target, pace and history.

The schema has no separate start_date: existing goal-start semantics derive the local day from created_at. Offline replay carries weight, affected date and operation ID, not verified original submission time. Therefore a first replay after that day does not correct the historical baseline. Test this limitation, midnight/timezone boundaries, canonical units, body-fat-only/unrelated-day controls, retries, rollback, locking and client refresh. No dependency on PR436.

[Original requirements](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/446#issuecomment-6065172350) and [the preserved pre-implementation description](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/issues/446#issuecomment-6065685173) retain prior wording.

## Implementing Codex task

Current implementing task: `01a11c77-0cff-76e7-b21f-6f5702949026`, explicitly handed this distinct outcome after the prior goal/Daily Balance owner checkpointed. Prior owner: `01a1128c-d211-7497-8dbe-3acf0662f004`; its PR436 remains untouched.

## Implementing PR

[PR449](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/449) (draft). Existing PR436 addresses saved Daily Balance targets and is a separate outcome.

Restore saved targets in completed-day Daily Balance (#436)

## Summary

Completed days can show “Saved target unavailable” even when their
calorie target was saved: Daily Balance reads a single-day response that
drops the comparison returned by the calendar. This change returns the
validated saved comparison in day reads and phone/watch completion
acknowledgements, including their sync payloads. Existing snapshots
retain their original target; missing legacy history remains
unavailable.

Closes #435. Targets `master`; no unmerged dependency. No data repair,
migration or current-target substitution.

## Test plan and behavior evidence

| Scenario | Expected and observed |
| --- | --- |
| Read a completed day with 1,800 kcal intake and a saved 2,000 target |
The actual changed serializer and app show **200 kcal remaining**; the
actual base shows unavailable. |
| Complete today, refetch and reload while the current plan differs |
Three maintained browser cases pass, including switching from the
current 2,100 target to saved 2,000 and retaining it after reload.
Backend route tests verify acknowledgement, read and sync consistency. |
| Missing legacy snapshot or older payload without the optional field |
Remains unavailable after reload. Backend tests also preserve snapshots
through goal changes/recompletion and reject partial snapshots and
invalid totals. |

### Before / After

Actual base `4cbcbc74` → captured source `3ac32ffa`. Current head
`d94a34d0` only adds corrected API description/generated comments;
runtime behavior and captures are unchanged. Independently built Windows
Chrome apps, identical synthetic fixtures and 390×844 viewport; these
are browser captures, not physical-device evidence. API fixtures below
are generated by each revision's actual serializer. [Exact
source/build/fixture provenance and
hashes](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/README.md).

**Valid saved target: the day becomes comparable again.**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: saved target
unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/before-valid.png)
| ![After: 200 kcal
remaining](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/after-valid.png)
|

**Missing snapshot: historical values are not invented.**

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: missing
snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/before-missing.png)
| ![After: still
unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/7dd85c054275e336e1c42ff3b85ec6442d426c67/after-missing.png)
|

## Supporting checks and limitations

Local validation passed: 764 backend tests, 53 focused client tests,
backend typecheck, independent baseline/current web builds, three
browser regressions and four capture cases. Evidence is retained outside
the product history; the PR has two scoped commits and ten files,
including the required API description/generated mirror.

No live database, user OTA or physical-device run. Actual deployed
versions and the affected records' snapshot state remain unverified.
Unrelated transient PWA notices were suppressed consistently during
capture. GitHub-page rendering verification is waived; genuine
pixel/provenance and independent QA requirements remain. [Bot review was
quota-refused](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/pull/436#issuecomment-6029479109)
on the captured source; no completed bot review is claimed. Independent
QA remains required.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Read the timezone again after acquiring the planning lock**

Use the transactionally current `User.timezone` for this eligibility check. The `timeZone` variable was hydrated before the transaction, but a concurrent profile update can change the timezone, commit, and release this same user-row lock before the metric continues; `acceptedToday` and `createdLocalDate` are then calculated in the former timezone and can rewrite the baseline on the wrong account-local day. Fetch the timezone through `tx` after the lock and derive both dates from that value.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L159-L162](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/eb142dd0bcc527398e83b91d29d4514fd9b4e516/AGENTS.md#L159-L162)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply the planning lock before every competing metric write**

Standardize this lock-first ordering in the other weight writers before introducing it here. For example, a concurrent Wear `metric.upsert` in `backend/src/services/watch.ts:359-385` locks the same `BodyMetric` row and only afterward calls `markCurrentCaloriePlanForReviewIfUnsafe`, which locks the user row; this handler now locks the user first and later upserts that metric row. When both update the same day, each transaction can wait for the other's lock and PostgreSQL aborts one as a deadlock, surfaced by both routes as a 500.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 70e982f77752400d4b4f688280a0609a99713262. The route now rereads User.timezone through tx after the planning lock and uses it for goal/acceptance dates, implicit metric date and future-date validation. Hosted PostgreSQL run 37824272218 passes forced profile-before-metric overlap in both LA/UTC directions with explicit and omitted dates, plus stable receipt replay. Original same-day/no-history-rewrite boundaries remain intact.

Fixed in 70e982f77752400d4b4f688280a0609a99713262. Wear metric upserts now take the planning guard before the metric read/write; weight imports had the same inverse order and now also lock first. Onboarding already locks the user first. Hosted PostgreSQL run 37824272218 passes forced web/Wear overlap in both writer orders, preserves Wear stale-revision 409 and receipt replay, and confirms the final metric without deadlock.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply baseline correction to Wear weight writes**

When a user creates a goal and then enters or corrects that local day's weight from Wear, this branch now acquires the planning lock but only updates `BodyMetric`; it never updates the current goal's `start_weight_grams` or emits the corresponding goal sync change. This leaves goal progress and projections dependent on whether the same correction was submitted through the web/mobile metric endpoint, contrary to the same-day behavior documented in `docs/goal-starting-weight.md`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply baseline correction to imported current-day weights**

When a Lose It import creates today's weight after today's goal was created, or overwrites today's existing weight, this transaction serializes the writer but never aligns the goal's starting weight with the imported metric. The newly documented same-day invariant therefore remains broken for imports, leaving a stale baseline and incorrect progress until another correction is submitted through `POST /metrics`.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 61b8dfc433d09532169e03b91a1482495c3b5a83. Wear now uses the shared same-day baseline correction and emits the goal sync event after safety evaluation within its idempotent transaction. PostgreSQL run 37825529039 passes both writer orders, one Wear goal event, persisted baseline, historical negative control, stale revision conflict and receipt replay.

Fixed in 61b8dfc433d09532169e03b91a1482495c3b5a83. Import create/overwrite uses the same baseline correction and final-state goal sync in the weight transaction, only for a current-day weight actually written. PostgreSQL run 37825529039 exercises the actual import route and ZIP parser: create and overwrite correct the baseline; KEEP, historical rows and identical repeat preserve it without duplicate goal events; completed food history is unchanged.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Repartition imported weights using the locked timezone**

When an import crosses local midnight or a concurrent profile update changes the account timezone, `today` reflects the transaction-current timezone but `boundedWeights.eligible` was already partitioned using the earlier authenticated-user snapshot. Consequently, a weight that is now today's can remain classified as future and be skipped, or a date that is now tomorrow can be imported without correcting the baseline; the returned counts and warnings are stale as well. Repartition the parsed weights after acquiring the lock and reading `currentUser.timezone`.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L159-L162](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/61b8dfc433d09532169e03b91a1482495c3b5a83/AGENTS.md#L159-L162)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 521fc625824259ec1236b664301c02bea1b516f6. Execute now partitions parsed weights after the planning lock and transaction-current timezone read; skipped counts and warnings come from that same result. PostgreSQL run 37826423169 passes forced timezone overlap in both directions for both candidate dates, checking eligibility, accepted/skipped counts, future warnings and the baseline. Six affected import tests and backend typecheck pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Revalidate Wear dates after taking the planning lock**

When a Wear mutation is parsed just before a concurrent timezone change, its future-date check uses the authenticated user's old timezone; this code then rereads the transaction-current timezone but proceeds without comparing `mutation.metricDate` with `today`. For example, near midnight a change from UTC (October 9) to America/Los_Angeles (October 8) can commit first, after which an October 9 weight is persisted as a future `BodyMetric` and omitted from current-day planning. Reapply the future-date validation using the locked `today`, as the metrics and import paths do.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L159-L162](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/521fc625824259ec1236b664301c02bea1b516f6/AGENTS.md#L159-L162)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in f805e6872c94000156219ddba0e8e01b0c8d490c. Wear rechecks metricDate against the transaction-current today immediately after the lock/timezone read, before any metric read or write. PostgreSQL run 37827497809 passes a forced UTC-to-LA overlap: a previously parsed October 9 mutation is rejected as future, metric/goal/sync remain unchanged, and retry after switching back to UTC preserves the original rejection. Fourteen affected tests and backend typecheck also pass.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Defer Wear date rejection until the locked timezone is known**

Fresh evidence in the current tree shows that `parseWatchMutation` still returns 400 at lines 154-156 before this post-lock check can run. If authentication captured `America/Los_Angeles` on October 8 and a concurrent profile update commits `UTC` on October 9, a valid October 9 Wear weight is rejected as future using the stale timezone and never reaches the transaction-current timezone read here. Parse the date syntactically first and perform the future-day comparison only after acquiring the planning lock.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L159-L162](https://github.com/MChartier/calibrate-health/blob/f805e6872c94000156219ddba0e8e01b0c8d490c/AGENTS.md#L159-L162)

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

Fixed in 650862e1c13be66fe5ec05495320cc66ac32f8bb. The parser now validates only date syntax; future-day eligibility is decided exclusively after the planning lock and current timezone read. PostgreSQL run 37828422760 passes both directions: newly future dates reject without writes, and dates parsed under LA that become current after UTC commits are accepted with one baseline sync event and stable receipt replay. Fourteen affected Wear tests and backend typecheck pass.

commit.message: Fix same-day goal baseline after weight corrections
Use current timezone and consistent metric writer lock order
Apply same-day baseline correction to Wear and imported weights
Classify imported weight dates after acquiring the planning lock
Revalidate Wear metric dates after the planning lock
Defer Wear calendar eligibility to the locked transaction

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,28 @@
+# Same-day goal starting weight
+
+A weight entered or corrected on the current goal's first local day also corrects
+its starting weight. The goal ID, start day, target, pace and calorie-plan history
+stay intact. Weights retain the existing tenth-of-a-unit input precision and
+canonical gram storage. An unsafe corrected plan uses the existing review state;
+the correction does not silently change its target or pace.
+
+The existing model has no separate start-date field. The start day is the local
+date of `Goal.created_at` in the user's timezone, as used by Progress and
+calibration. Correction requires that start day, the metric's date and the current
+user-local day all match after acquiring the calorie-planning lock.
+The timezone is reread inside that transaction after the lock, so a profile
+change that commits first determines eligibility and the default metric date.
+Wear and import weight writers acquire the same guard before metric rows to
+avoid reversing the lock order against normal corrections.
+Accepted Wear writes and imported current-day weights use the same correction
+and goal-sync rule. Imports that KEEP an existing weight, body-fat-only updates
+and historical import rows do not change the baseline.
+
+Offline weight intent remains `{ weight, date }` plus its stable operation ID.
+Until accepted, the app shows the pending metric and retains the server-owned
+goal; calorie targets/projections remain marked as syncing. Replay refreshes the
+goal query. A first replay after the start day saves the metric but leaves the
+older baseline unchanged: there is no verified original-submission day in this
+protocol. Retrying an already committed operation returns its original receipt
+without overwriting later corrections. Historical edits, body-fat-only updates
+and other goals are not baseline corrections.
